Recognize the approach

Pixel-based graphic styles turn the image grid into a visible part of the design.

Look for

  • Hard-edged silhouettes
  • Limited palettes
  • Details aligned to an image grid

Your learning goal

Describe the visual decisions before choosing a tool. Then make one small example that uses them deliberately.

Next: Origins

Where it comes from

Pixel-based graphic styles turn the image grid into a visible part of the design. Small icons and tightly controlled details were common in parts of the early web, alongside many non-pixel styles.

Period or influence
1990s–2000s web visibility

What to examine

Look at the heading, one control, the image treatment, and the reading order. Explain which decisions establish the style and which make the page usable.

Next: Construction

How to construct it

  1. Draw at a small native resolution and preview at the intended display size.
  2. Scale by whole-number factors when preserving hard pixels. Keep paragraph text separate from decorative bitmap lettering.

Small practice task

Draw one 24-by-24 icon with a four-color palette. Test it at its native size and twice that size.

Before you expand it

Test the result at its intended size, on a narrow screen, and with keyboard focus. Preserve editable layers and record the source and license of acquired assets.
